events.excerpt: Hi all, Happy to launch private.zecblock.com , a version of ZecBlock where the server doesn’t learn what you look up. ZecBlock Private uses PIR (Private Information Retrieval) . How it works Your browser encrypts the search before sending it. The transaction ID, block or address never leaves your device in readable form. The server works through the whole dataset to answer, without knowing which record you asked for. It sends back one encrypted answer, and only your browser can decrypt it. A search for something that exists looks the same as a search for something that doesn’t. As far as we know, it’s the first full block explorer (transactions, blocks and addresses) built on PIR. Previous PIR explorer demos covered narrower lookups, such as address balances. Check it yourself Open your browser’s developer tools (Inspect → Network) and search for something. Every request of the same kind is the same size, and none of them contains what you typed. After each search, the site also shows a short summary of exactly what your browser sent. Details Data stays close to the chain tip: new blocks are published every few seconds, typically within about 20 seconds of the regular explorer. Each data publication is signed, and your browser checks every result against it. Searches are heavier
events.headline: ZecBlock Private: look up transactions, blocks and addresses with PIR

He calls Bitcoin “all hype,” with no intrinsic value, income, or dividends, and says much of the supply now sits with ETF investors and Bitcoin treasury companies rather than people who want to use it as money. events.excerpt: A Zcash governance trilogy, part 3 of 3. Or navigating the dark forest without turning on all the lights TL;DR: In a private system we cannot know who holds voting power, how many people sit behind it, or whom they are connected to. The answer is not to abolish the privacy. It is to bound what any vote can decide, so that capturing one voting mechanism cannot confer control over the whole system. Part 1 : An Ode to Rough Consensus . Part 2 : When We Disagree: Making Rough Consensus Work . Part 3 : Governance in a Shielded World. Zcash is building a parallel financial system, outside of but adjacent to the existing one. Its governance, however, remains entirely inside human institutions. That private financial system starts from a different assumption from the one we have become accustomed to elsewhere: privacy is normal. In such a system, private by default should be the ordinary situation, not a special mode for people with something to hide. Traditional finance already runs part of its markets this way. Dark pools let large investors trade without displaying their orders, so that others cannot trade against them. Dark does not mean lawless. events.excerpt: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article
events.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash

events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Has Fully Covered the $6.34 Billion Hack With Company Funds Binance said Thursday it has completed coverage of the $6.34 billion Oct. 29 hack from company funds, two weeks after the largest crypto theft on record, even as withdrawals continue to reopen in phases. In a Thursday announcement, the exchange wrote that it “has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident” and published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot. It repeated the same message on X. That wording matters. Coverage means Binance has replaced the affected tokens from its own books, not that it has recovered the stolen coins from the attackers. The exchange said it committed more than $6.34 billion in company funds and bought the affected tokens through market and over-the-counter channels, drawing on a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of its futures insurance fund above the level required under its risk-management framework, and its corporate treasury. Binance has also committed to replenishing SAFU to about $1 billion after that partial draw, a step it said would keep the fund fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve. events.excerpt: We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird's blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers , and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy. As previously reported , Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He's been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year. The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “ Planet Claire ” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on " raygun ," of course).
events.headline: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn

events.excerpt: This Node and Miner patch release is recommended for all node operators and storage providers. Review the upgrade warning before upgrading. ✨ Notable Changes ⚠️ Upgrade warning: Ethereum JSON-RPC rejects negative, unprefixed, leading-zero and oversized (>256-bit) big integers. Security: wasmtime 48 is a long-term-support release that gets security fixes until ~August 2028. Performance: on a mainnet node over 24 hours, median execution time per unit of gas fell about 18% for messages and 11% overall, with no regressions seen on mainnet or calibnet ( measurements ). events.excerpt: For 11 years, a Massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way. But through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: He was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or AAS). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it's primarily used to beef up cows. Left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like. Read full article Comments
events.headline: Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart

events.headline: Software Samaritan revamps borked Indian certs to block smart TV ads

events.excerpt: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that's due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane. Read full article Comments
events.headline: The amazing disappearing exoplanet

events.excerpt: Description A few small nit cleanups on the synchronizer component in consensus. Behavior change: fetch_blocks_from_peers now returns as soon as no request is in flight, instead of idling until the 4s FETCH_FROM_PEERS_TIMEOUT. This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. In both cases no further network request is sent, and a failed request still waits the full 2s request timeout, so periodic runs cannot repeat faster than every ~2s on failures. The only new cost is local: while all selected blocks are locked, the scheduler polls get_missing_blocks at its default 200ms cadence instead of every 4s, which is the same cadence it already uses during fast successful sync. Added a test covering both cases. Test plan CI/PT Release notes Check each box that your changes affect. If none of the boxes relate to your changes, release notes aren't required. For each box you select, include information after the relevant heading that describes the impact of your changes that a user might notice and any actions they must take to implement updates. The issue affects images rendered with a height or width of zero at the selected printing resolution. These might not be visible to users, but can form part of a document's watermarking or layout. After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too. Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected." According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016. Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected. Users need not have added these objects themselves. Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible.
